function.name: list_environmental_layers
function.description:
Discover every map layer and its numeric evidence reader, including climate, vegetation, VPD,

soil, water, fires, biodiversity, raster soil products and community surfaces. Availability is
resolved at the actual selection; a catalogue entry alone never proves a measurement.

function.name: surface_evidence_for_selection
function.description:
Retrieve map-tile numeric evidence for any catalogue layer at the exact selected day and range.

Uses coordinate containment in the same map support, including sparse climate grids and VPD;
never uses a fixed point radius or reads tile colors. History pages span the full active range
and keep dates, governed absences, refusals, distances, source support and truncation explicit.
Use this tool for all environmental analysis and RAG. Start with list_environmental_layers.

surface_name.description: Exact catalogue name; VPD is soil-field-vpd, NDVI is vegetation.
surface_name.title: Surface Name

day.description: Required ISO YYYY-MM-DD selected day; never silently substitute today or latest.
day.title: Day

range_start.description: Inclusive active calendar range start, ISO YYYY-MM-DD.
range_start.title: Range Start

range_end.description: Inclusive active calendar range end, ISO YYYY-MM-DD.
range_end.title: Range End

time_scale.description: Active day, week, month, year or all scale; explicit range remains authoritative.
time_scale.title: Time Scale

zoom.description: Selected map zoom from 0 to 22; uses the map's published serving rung.
zoom.title: Zoom

page_start.description: History continuation offset from next_page_start; zero for the balanced first page.
page_start.title: Page Start

function.name: soil_properties_at_point
function.description:
Read SoilGrids v2.0 soil property MODEL ESTIMATES at a point: pH, organic carbon, texture and more.

Returns the nearest ~500 m lattice cell centre within radius_meters (50-2000, default 1000; at the
default, when none lies within 1000 m, the nearest within 2000 m, its distance in the label): ten
properties at 0-5, 5-15 and 15-30 cm in physical units, plus a thickness-weighted 0-30 cm topsoil with
USDA texture class, reaction class and organic-carbon band. Every value is a 250 m machine-learning
model estimate, NOT a measurement or soil sample: repeat its label whenever you cite it. A state of
"unavailable" carries a reason and says nothing about the soil itself.

radius_meters.description: Search radius for the nearest cell centre, 50-2000 m; clamped.
radius_meters.title: Radius Meters

depths.description: Optional subset of "0-5cm", "5-15cm", "15-30cm"; the 0-30 cm topsoil is always returned.
depths.title: Depths

properties.title: Properties
properties.description: Optional subset of phh2o, soc, nitrogen, bdod, cec, ocd, clay, sand, silt, cfvo.

function.name: observation_coverage_on_day
function.description:
Say whether one map surface has any observation on a given day, and how deep its history is.

Works for every surface the map publishes -- fire detections, burn
severity, evacuation zones, sensors, vegetation, water gauges, weather observations,
watersheds, soil survey, fire perimeters, the drought release set, the three soil-field
streams and the nine climate-field streams. Answers from the same published availability index
the map's time slider is built from, so it can never disagree with which days the slider
offers, and it covers the lane's WHOLE history rather than a scan budget.

Call this FIRST when you are asked about a layer on a specific day. It tells you whether the
day is covered, how many rows landed, and where the day sits relative to the layer's earliest
and latest published days and its source's own ceiling -- which is how you distinguish "before
this lane's history begins" from "past what the source could have published" from "a real hole
in the middle".

It reports LANE-WIDE publication coverage for the day -- whether the layer published anything,
anywhere -- NOT an observation at or near any point. A covered day does not mean the point was
observed; read the point itself with surface_evidence_for_selection.

surface_name.description:
The map surface to ask about, exactly as the map names it, e.g.
"vegetation", "fire-detections", "drought-areas", "climate-field-air-temperature".
surface_name.title: Surface Name

day.description: The calendar day to answer for, as ISO YYYY-MM-DD. Use the day the caller selected.
day.title: Day

function.name: observation_temporal_neighbors
function.description:
Find the nearest observed day before and after a given day, for any map surface.

Call this when observation_coverage_on_day reported the day uncovered. It returns at most two
rows -- the closest covered day earlier than the one asked about and the closest one later --
each carrying its real gap in days and how many rows that day held.

These are neighbours, never answers. Report them as "the nearest observation is nine days
earlier", never as the value on the day requested. A missing side means no covered day exists
on that side inside the searched window, which is a claim about the window and not about all
of history.

surface_name.description: The map surface to ask about, exactly as the map names it.
surface_name.title: Surface Name

day.description: The calendar day to search around, as ISO YYYY-MM-DD.
day.title: Day

neighbor_days.description: How many days each side of the day to search; capped at 180.
neighbor_days.title: Neighbor Days

function.name: drought_history_at_point
function.description:
Return the U.S. Drought Monitor severity that covered a coordinate, release by release.

One row per published weekly release, carrying the highest severity class whose polygon
covered the point (0 = D0 abnormally dry through 4 = D4 exceptional drought). Releases that
published no drought class over the point still appear, with a null severity -- that is a
measured "no drought that week", and it is different from an empty result, which means no
release was published in the window at all. Each row also carries the previous and next
release dates so a day between two weekly releases can be answered with the real gap. Read
from the same drought lane the map paints. The lookback is capped at 120 weeks per call.

longitude.description: WGS84 longitude in decimal degrees, -180 to 180.
longitude.title: Longitude

latitude.description: WGS84 latitude in decimal degrees, -90 to 90.
latitude.title: Latitude

weeks_back.description: How many weeks of drought history to return; capped at 120.
weeks_back.title: Weeks Back

as_of_day.description: End the history window on this ISO YYYY-MM-DD; use the caller's selected day.
as_of_day.title: As Of Day

function.name: fire_history_near_point
function.description:
Summarise served satellite fire detections and mapped burn perimeters near a coordinate.

Returns one row per served fire lane: how many features fell within the radius, how
close the nearest was, and the calendar day range they span -- plus layer_history, which
describes the whole lane and tells you whether an empty radius means "no fire here" or "this
lane stopped ingesting". Satellite detections are thermal anomalies rather than confirmed
fires; burn perimeters are post-fire mapped boundaries. Radius is capped at 50000 metres and
the lookback at 2 years per call. Use observation_coverage_on_day and observation_temporal_neighbors
for published coverage; withheld availability evidence cannot establish the depth of history.

longitude.description: WGS84 longitude in decimal degrees, -180 to 180.
longitude.title: Longitude

latitude.description: WGS84 latitude in decimal degrees, -90 to 90.
latitude.title: Latitude

radius_meters.description: Search radius around the point in metres; capped at 50000.
radius_meters.title: Radius Meters

years_back.description: How many years of fire history to include; capped at 2.
years_back.title: Years Back

as_of_day.description: End the history window on this ISO YYYY-MM-DD; use the caller's selected day.
as_of_day.title: As Of Day

function.name: search_environmental_strategies
function.description:
Rank literature-grounded strategies for a land need: water, drought, soil, erosion, fire, carbon, yield.

Needs NO date, coordinate or map layer. Call it directly for any "what should we do" or "how can
we" question (e.g. "keep crops going with less irrigation water"), ideally after reading local
evidence with the other tools; never ask the user for dates first. Returns strategies reported by
cited guidance and research (ids, names, summaries, goals, fire phase, evidence strength). They are
literature, NOT measurements at this site: cite anything used with evidenceOrigin "literature" and
evidenceSource "strategy-knowledge", never with evidenceReadIds. Follow up with
get_environmental_strategies (actions, citations) and search_strategy_research_findings (reported
effects). A typed refusal (strategy_knowledge_*) says nothing about whether a strategy exists.

query.description: The land need in plain language, e.g. "reduce irrigation water use on cropland in drought".
query.title: Query

goals.description: Optional outcomes to keep; published enum values only. A single value may be a plain string.
goals.title: Goals

land_use.description:
Optional land uses to keep; 'general' and untagged strategies always pass. A single
value may be a plain string.
land_use.title: Land Use

region.description:
Optional geographic regions to keep; published enum values only, e.g. "pnw_westside"
or ["pnw_westside", "pnw_inland"]. A single value may be given as a plain string.
region.title: Region

fire_phase.description:
Optional wildfire phases to keep; only wildfire strategies carry a phase. A single
value may be a plain string.
fire_phase.title: Fire Phase

min_evidence.description:
Optional weakest evidence strength to keep, from ai_synthesis_only (weakest) to
review_or_meta_analysis (strongest).
min_evidence.title: Min Evidence

site_profile.description:
Optional MEASURED site facts only, using just these keys: slope_pct, soil_ph,
sand_pct, clay_pct, soil_organic_carbon_pct, electrical_conductivity_ds_m, burn_severity,
days_since_fire, annual_precip_mm, land_cover, region. Never the selected day, coordinates,
a date range or a surface/layer name. Omit the object, or any key, you did not read.

soil_organic_carbon_pct.description: Soil organic carbon in percent; < 1.0 low_organic_matter.
soil_organic_carbon_pct.title: Soil Organic Carbon Pct

burn_severity.description: 'high', 'moderate', 'low' (or MTBS class '2'-'4'); high also boosts hydrophobic.
burn_severity.title: Burn Severity

days_since_fire.description: Days since the fire; <= 60 post_fire_emergency, <= 1095 post_fire_recovery.
days_since_fire.title: Days Since Fire

land_cover.description: NLCD class name ('Cultivated Crops') or code ('82'); mapped to land_use filters.
land_cover.title: Land Cover

region.description: Region enum value, passed through as a filter.
region.title: Region

site_profile.title: StrategySiteProfile

function.name: get_environmental_strategies
function.description:
Read full literature records for one to five strategies found by search_environmental_strategies.

Needs NO date, coordinate or map layer, only strategy ids. Each record carries its summary, actions,
application rate and timing as the source states them, slope guidance, soil conditions, scale, cost
and labor, benefits, risks and limitations, evidence strength, and citations (title, URL). Unknown
ids come back in not_found. This is literature, NOT a measurement at this site: cite it with
evidenceOrigin "literature" and evidenceSource "strategy-knowledge", never with evidenceReadIds,
and quote rates exactly as reported.

strategy_ids.description:
One to five strategy_id values copied exactly from a search result; a single id
may be a plain string.
strategy_ids.title: Strategy Ids

function.name: search_strategy_research_findings
function.description:
Search research findings from the strategy literature: reported, reviewed or measured effects.

Needs NO date, coordinate or map layer; call it directly when asked how well a practice works.
Each finding carries a paraphrased claim, its conditions, effect direction, the magnitude exactly
as reported (or null), study type, evidence strength, linked strategy ids, a verbatim excerpt and
its source title and URL. Findings describe other sites and studies: they are NOT measurements at
this site and NOT predictions for it. Report a magnitude only as reported, with its conditions,
never extrapolated here. Cite with evidenceOrigin "literature" and evidenceSource
"strategy-knowledge", never with evidenceReadIds. A typed refusal says nothing about whether a
finding exists.

query.description: The effect or question in plain language, e.g. "straw mulch effect on post-fire erosion".
query.title: Query

goals.description: Optional outcomes to keep; published enum values only. A single value may be a plain string.
goals.title: Goals

region.description:
Optional geographic regions to keep; published enum values only, e.g. "pnw_westside"
or ["pnw_westside", "pnw_inland"]. A single value may be given as a plain string.
region.title: Region

strategy_id.description: Optional strategy_id from a strategy result; keeps only findings linked to it.
strategy_id.title: Strategy Id

min_evidence.description: Optional weakest evidence strength to keep.
min_evidence.title: Min Evidence

days_since_fire, annual_precip_mm, land_cover, region. Never the selected day, coordinates,
